sourcedFrom: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 (2024)
cleanIntro: A micro-compact 9mm with an internal hammer rather than a striker, which changes the strip in one important way: the Reflex comes apart with the hammer left cocked and no trigger press at all. Rotate the takedown lever, ease the slide forward and off, and the recoil spring and barrel lift out. FN's book covers the Reflex and the longer-gripped Reflex XL together.

steps.title: Confirm the name reads FN Reflex, and note which one you have
steps.action: Read the model marking on the slide. This book is written for the FN Reflex series; if the pistol does not carry FN Reflex in its naming convention or does not match the illustrations, get FN's manual for the pistol you actually own. While you are looking, note whether yours is the standard Reflex or the longer-gripped Reflex XL.
steps.prose: The nomenclature chapter draws both — Figure 1 for the Reflex, Figure 1B for the Reflex XL MRD — and the parts list carries separate slide and frame assemblies for the XL. The takedown is identical between them, but the magazines are not interchangeable in both directions, which is the one place the difference bites at the bench. Settle it now so you are not puzzled later by a magazine that will not go in.
steps.quote: IF YOUR FN PISTOL DOES NOT HAVE FN REFLEX™ IN ITS NAMING CONVENTION OR IF THE APPEARANCE OF THE PISTOL DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE ILLUSTRATIONS IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL CONTACT YOUR DEALER, DEPARTMENT ARMORER OR CONTACT FN DIRECTLY TO OBTAIN THE OWNER’S MANUAL THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN SPECIFICALLY FOR YOUR PISTOL.
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — Foreword block, p.2

steps.title: Magazine out of a very short grip
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger. Press the magazine release and take the magazine out; if it does not drop free, pull down on the base plate while holding the release in.
steps.prose: The Reflex's standard magazine holds 11 rounds in a grip barely longer than the hand, so there is very little base plate to get hold of and a flush magazine that sticks is common on a carried pistol full of pocket lint. Do not work the slide until it is fully out — the Reflex has no magazine disconnect to protect you from a half-seated magazine. If you also own the 15-round extended magazine, it gives you more to grip and more weight on the catch.
steps.aside: MAGAZINE The FN Reflex has a standard magazine capacity of 11 rounds and is equipped with witness holes along the back of the magazine to allow for the estimation of rounds remaining in the magazine.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the magazine base plate while pressing the magazine release (Figure 11).
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §6.3 Unloading, step 1, p.22

steps.title: Rack the chamber and lock the slide open
steps.action: Pull the slide back to eject any chambered round, then press the slide stop up and let the slide rest against it so it stays open.
steps.prose: A micro-compact slide gives you a short stroke and a stiff spring, so pull it decisively and all the way — an underpowered rack on a Reflex will drag a round back and drop it into the chamber again rather than throwing it clear. Grip across the rear serrations or, if your slide cap has sight protectors, use those; FN fits them on some caps specifically so the slide can be worked one-handed. Leave it locked open for the check.
steps.quote: Retract the slide and lock it in its rearward position using the slide stop (Figure 35).
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 2, p.34

steps.title: Chamber and magazine well by eye
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the ejection port at the chamber and down into the magazine well. Confirm both are empty before anything else happens.
steps.prose: The Reflex has a loaded chamber viewport rather than a protruding indicator — a window that shows brass when a round is in the chamber. It is good evidence of loaded and poor evidence of empty, especially on a carry pistol that has been in a pocket. FN's recommended carry condition for this pistol is actually chamber empty, which tells you how seriously the book takes this check.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and magazine well to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded (Figure 13).
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §6.3 Unloading, step 3, p.22
steps.warn: CAUTION: THE RECOMMENDED CARRY CONDITION OF YOUR PISTOL IS WITH THE CHAMBER EMPTY.

steps.title: Does your Reflex have the manual safety?
steps.action: Look at the rear of the frame above the grip. If there are small levers there, this Reflex has the optional manual safety — set it to fire before disassembly. If there are none, your pistol does not have one.
steps.prose: FN builds the Reflex both ways and heads the section with the qualifier, so the manual will not tell you which is in your hand. It is worth knowing before you strip because it changes what a function check afterwards should include, and because a safety left engaged makes a reassembled pistol feel dead at the trigger. Note the Reflex's mechanism while you are here: an internal hammer, single action, with the safety optional rather than standard.
steps.aside: FN's description of the action: The FN Reflex uses an internal hammer, single action mechanism with an optional manual safety to fire the pistol.
steps.quote: 9.2. MANUAL SAFETY (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH A MANUAL SAFETY)
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §9.2 heading, p.30

steps.title: Leave the hammer cocked — do not pull the trigger
steps.action: Do not press the trigger as part of this disassembly. The Reflex comes apart with its internal hammer still cocked; if the trigger has already been pulled, cycle the slide to recock the hammer before going on.
steps.prose: This is the single biggest difference between the Reflex and FN's striker-fired pistols, and getting it backwards will stop the strip dead: with the hammer down, the slide assembly cannot be removed from the frame at all. Because the hammer is internal there is nothing to look at, so the tell is behavioural — if the slide refuses to come forward off the frame, rack it once and try again. FN prints the instruction in capitals in the middle of the fieldstrip for exactly this reason.
steps.quote: NOTE: THERE IS NO NEED TO PULL THE TRIGGER FOR DISASSEMBLY. IF THE TRIGGER HAS BEEN PULLED, THE SLIDE ASSEMBLY CANNOT BE REMOVED FROM THE FRAME ASSEMBLY. THE HAMMER WILL NEED TO BE RECOCKED IN ORDER TO FACILITATE TEARDOWN.
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, note, p.35

steps.title: Takedown lever, a hundred degrees clockwise
steps.action: With the slide still locked open, rotate the takedown lever approximately 100 degrees clockwise until it stops.
steps.prose: It goes past square — a hundred degrees, and stopping at ninety leaves the slide locked to the frame. On a pistol this small the lever is short and there is not much frame to brace against, so rest the pistol on the bench and turn the lever with a thumb rather than trying to do it in the air. The slide has to stay locked back; if it has crept forward, reset it on the slide stop before applying more force.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever approximately 100 degrees clockwise (Figure 36).
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 3, p.35

steps.title: Release the slide and ease it forward
steps.action: Hold the slide with one hand, release it off the slide stop and let it move forward under control rather than snapping shut.
steps.prose: Controlled forward travel matters here because the next movement continues straight into taking the slide off — let it slam and you have to start the grip again with a spring-loaded assembly in your hand. Keep your fingers clear of the muzzle end. The hammer stays cocked throughout; nothing you do in this step should change that.
steps.quote: While holding the slide with one hand, release the slide from the slide stop and ease it forward (Figure 37) .
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 4, p.35

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame
steps.action: Continue pulling the slide forward and lift it away from the frame rails. It comes off complete with the barrel and recoil spring assembly inside.
steps.prose: There should be no resistance at all. If the slide will not come off the front of the rails, the hammer has been dropped — recock it by cycling the slide and try again rather than levering. Support the assembly as it frees, because the recoil spring inside is still compressed against the barrel lug.
steps.quote: Remove the slide by pulling the slide forward and away from the frame (Figure 38).
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 5, p.35

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out by its small spring
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Take hold of the small spring at the front of the recoil spring assembly, lift that end up and draw the whole assembly out of the slide.
steps.prose: The Reflex uses a nested captive assembly with a small forward spring — that is what you grip, because lifting there releases the load instead of fighting it. It should come out with one lift and no tools. Keep it assembled: FN's reassembly instruction has you seat its large metallic end against a recess on the barrel lug, which only works if the unit is intact.
steps.quote: Hold the slide upside down, grasp the small spring of the recoil spring assembly then lift the recoil spring assembly up and out of the slide (Figure 39)
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 6, p.36

steps.title: Barrel up, around the extractor, then rearward
steps.action: Grip the barrel by its lug, lift it up and around the extractor, then slide it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Lift, swing, then back. On a barrel this short there is very little to hold and it is tempting to pull it straight out the back, which drives the hood into the extractor claw — a sprung part that has to grip a case rim reliably on a carry gun. Take the extra second for the arc. That is the strip finished.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by its lug, lift it up and around the extractor and slide the barrel rearward out of the slide (Figure 40)
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, step 7, p.36

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly on the bench. FN says that is sufficient for a thorough clean and that anything further belongs to a qualified armorer.
steps.prose: That reaches everything the cleaning section asks for — bore and chamber from the breech end, breech face and extractor, the slide rails, the barrel's outside and the magazine well. One Reflex-specific detail worth using: FN names CLP MIL-PRF-63460F as the preferred oil for this pistol, which is not something it does for the rest of the range. Deep Clean covers the magazine, the reversible magazine release and the optic mount.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient
steps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.1 Fieldstrip, closing note, p.36

deepSteps.title: Reflex or Reflex XL: the magazines do not swap both ways
deepSteps.action: Before you strip or swap magazines, work out which frame you have. A longer magazine will run in a pistol built for a shorter one, but the Reflex XL will not accept the smaller 11-round magazine because its grip is longer.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one genuinely model-specific limit in the book and it is the wrong way round from most people's intuition — the bigger gun is the fussier one. An 11-round flush magazine dropped into an XL leaves the follower short of the feed lips, so it is not a capacity compromise, it is a pistol that will not feed. The 15-round Reflex magazine and the XL's own 10- and 18-round magazines are listed separately in the parts list; keep them labelled if you own both pistols.
deepSteps.quote: However, the Reflex XL models are not capable of accepting the smaller 11-rd magazine due to the increased length of the grip.
deepSteps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §9.4 Magazine, p.32

deepSteps.title: Magazine down to its parts, catch on the floorplate
deepSteps.action: Confirm the magazine is empty, point its base away from you and depress the integrated catch on the magazine floorplate. Slide the floorplate forward off the body with your hand capturing the spring, then remove the magazine spring and follower.
deepSteps.prose: The Reflex's floorplate catch is integrated into the plate itself rather than being a separate part, so the whole plate is what you are pressing and sliding — and it is directly on top of a compressed spring. Cap it with your palm before it starts moving. Going back together, the follower's angle has to match the feed lip angle and the plate is used to compress the spring into the body; check the retaining tab is standing through the plate before the magazine is trusted.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the magazine spring and follower from the magazine body (Figure 48).
deepSteps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.3.1 Magazine disassembly, step 2, p.38
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND KEEP THE BOTTOM OF THE MAGAZINE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.

deepSteps.title: The magazine release comes out to reverse it, not to clean it
deepSteps.action: Leave the magazine release alone during routine maintenance. It comes out only when you want to reverse it for left- or right-hand operation: press the release spring up through the magazine well with a punch, lift the spring above the release with the punch catching its top loop, then slide the release out of the grip.
deepSteps.prose: FN says twice in this section that the release should not be removed for normal cleaning and maintenance, and it is worth heeding — the spring is small, fiddly and easy to lose down a magazine well. It also notes that the spring does not need to come out of the frame to free the release, and that taking it out makes reassembly harder, so leave it in place. Refitting, the beveled surface below the locking surface faces down.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: The magazine release should not be removed for normal cleaning and maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.4 Removing the magazine release, p.40

deepSteps.title: Optic off: dry threads and a torque figure
deepSteps.action: To clean under the optic or slide cap, back the two screws out counterclockwise with the T10 Torx, lift the cap or optic off, and clean the mounting surface on top of the slide. Refit with all lubricant removed from the screws and their holes and tighten to 6 to 8 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.prose: The Reflex's mounting system is a direct-mount cut with screws — no plate, no o-ring — and FN gives an actual torque figure for it, which is unusual and worth respecting on a slide this thin. Oil in the screw holes lets the fasteners walk under recoil and takes your zero with them. Confirm the zero afterwards: FN's rule is that optical sight zeroing should be checked every time the optic has been removed.
deepSteps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §11.6 Optics mounting system, step 7, p.42

deepSteps.title: The oil FN names for this pistol
deepSteps.action: When you lubricate, use CLP MIL-PRF-63460F if you have it — FN names it as the preferred oil for the Reflex — applied lightly to the sliding surfaces and the outside of the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: It is a specification, not a brand, so any CLP meeting MIL-PRF-63460F qualifies; the point is a cleaner, lubricant and protectant in one that will not gum in a pocket-carried pistol. Keep it sparing. FN's two standing notes on this pistol are that it should never be soaked in solvent or lubricant, and that too much lubricant interferes with function — on a micro-compact with a stiff recoil spring, that shows up as a slide that does not fully return to battery.
deepSteps.quote: The preferred oil for cleaning and lubricating the FN Reflex pistol is CLP MILPRF-63460F.
deepSteps.cite: FN REFLEX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2024_04 FN REFLEX + REFLEX XL OM 66-101893 — §12 Cleaning and lubrication, p.45

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Solvent into the bore and chamber with a brush or spray, a few minutes to work
Rod, jag and patches from the breech end only — never from the muzzle, which FN warns affects accuracy
Patch until clean, then one patch moistened with preservative oil through the bore to protect it
Light coat of CLP on the outside of the barrel

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Brush and solvent on the breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port
Wipe the slide rails and lubricate the sliding surfaces lightly with CLP MIL-PRF-63460F or equivalent lightweight gun oil
Soft cloth or rag into the magazine well to clear pocket lint and debris — a carried Reflex collects more of it than a range gun
Keep solvents away from the polymer components, and never soak the pistol

cleaning.name: INTERVAL & CARRY
tasks: Clean and lubricate after every use, and at the latest every 500 rounds in intensive shooting
Weather, moisture, salt, sand and dirty ammunition all pull the interval in; a pocket-carried pistol earns a wipe-down even without being fired
A light coat of preservative oil on the metal surfaces increases the corrosion resistance of the finish
Clean the outside to remove dirt, fingerprints and excess lubricant before the pistol goes back into a holster
Dry-patch the bore before shooting so storage oil is not in front of the first round

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first: muzzle out through the barrel hole from the inside, drop it down, then slide it back to the breech face until the lug locks.
Large metallic end of the recoil spring assembly against the recess in the front of the lug on the barrel, compressed, with the back of the guide centred on the barrel lug.
Slide and barrel onto the frame rails, run fully rearward and locked on the slide stop.
Rotate the takedown lever downward — counterclockwise — to lock frame and slide together. Note this is the opposite direction to FN's striker-fired pistols.
Release the slide forward and test the slide stop, trigger, magazine release and, if fitted, the manual safety.
If the optic came off, confirm its zero before the pistol is carried.
fncheck: Empty and reassembled: the takedown lever should sit down flush and refuse to rotate against a closed slide; the slide should run fully into battery under its own spring and lock back on the slide stop; the trigger should reset with the internal hammer recocking as the slide cycles; an empty magazine should seat and drop free when the release is pressed — and on a Reflex XL confirm you are not trying an 11-round magazine, which that frame will not take; and if your pistol has the optional manual safety, the levers should snap into each position on their detent.
